intro: The nursery door slams behind you, and somewhere a lullaby starts to play in the shape of a checkout chime. Every toy in this room was delivered by Amazon, and each one has read the Conditions of Use far more closely than you ever did. To reach the door, you must prove you know what you agreed to.
verdict: Nearly all disputes with Amazon go to private, binding arbitration, and you give up class actions and jury trials.
Reviews, photos and videos you post can be used by Amazon forever, worldwide, and passed on to others for free.
You accept these terms on behalf of everyone in your household who uses your account.
Amazon can change the terms at any time, and continuing to use the service means you accept the changes.
Amazon may close your account, cancel orders or remove content at its sole discretion.

puzzles.quote: If customer service can’t resolve it and you wish to pursue arbitration, you must complete the dispute resolution procedure set forth here , including submitting a completed Notice of Dispute using this Claim Form and negotiating in good faith for 60 days.
puzzles.title: The Long Ride Nowhere
puzzles.question: For how many days must you negotiate in good faith with Amazon before you can start arbitration?
puzzles.riddle: Creak, creak, back and forth I go, carrying no rider anywhere at all. Tell me how many days a complaint must rock in place before it may gallop toward a ruling.
puzzles.plain_english: Before you can bring a formal claim against Amazon, you must contact customer service, file a Notice of Dispute, and then negotiate for 60 days. That means even a valid complaint is delayed by about two months.
hints: Look in the Disputes section, at the paragraph on what you must do before arbitration.
It is the number of days of good-faith negotiation after you submit your Notice of Dispute. Two months, give or take.

puzzles.clause_ref: Reviews, comments, communications, and other content
puzzles.quote: If you do post content or submit material, and unless we indicate otherwise, you grant Amazon a nonexclusive, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, and fully sublicensable right to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, publish, perform, translate, create derivative works from, distribute, and display such content throughout the world in any media.
puzzles.title: The Song That Never Ends
puzzles.question: How long does the licence you give Amazon over your reviews, photos and videos last?
puzzles.answer: Forever, and you cannot take it back
options: Forever, and you cannot take it back
puzzles.riddle: The ballerina turns to face you as the tune winds on and on. Every review you hum for them, they may play for as long as the box keeps spinning.
puzzles.plain_english: When you post a review, photo or video, you keep ownership, but Amazon gets a permanent, irrevocable, worldwide right to use, edit and pass on that content to others, without paying you. Deleting it later does not cancel that licence.
hints: Look in the section about reviews, comments and other content you post.
The licence is described as 'perpetual, irrevocable'. Which option matches those two words?

puzzles.quote: Amazon does sell products for children, but it sells them to adults, who can purchase with a credit card or other permitted payment method. If you are under 18, you may use the Amazon Services only with involvement of a parent or guardian.
puzzles.title: The Little Porcelain Customer
puzzles.question: Below what age may you use Amazon Services only with the involvement of a parent or guardian?
puzzles.riddle: I am small and cracked and have sat in this chair for ever so long, yet still they say I am too young to shop alone. How old must I be before no grown-up need hold my hand?
puzzles.plain_english: Amazon sells to adults. Anyone under 18 is only supposed to use the services with a parent or guardian involved, and a separate rule requires you to be 21 to buy alcohol.
hints: Look in the Your Account section, where children and parents are mentioned.
It is the age at which most people legally become adults, not the alcohol age.

puzzles.quote: By using the Amazon Services, you agree, on behalf of yourself and all members of your household and others who use any Amazon Service under your account, to the following conditions.
puzzles.title: Everyone Who Lives Here
puzzles.question: Besides yourself, on behalf of all members of your what do you agree to these conditions?
puzzles.riddle: Peer through my tiny windows: every little figure in every little room is bound by what you clicked. Name the place they all share.
puzzles.plain_english: When you accept these terms, Amazon treats you as agreeing for everyone in your home and anyone else using your account too. So family members using your account are covered by the same rules, including arbitration.
hints: Look at the very first paragraph, just after 'Welcome to Amazon.com'.
It is a single word for everyone who lives under your roof.

puzzles.quote: YOU AND WE AGREE THAT ANY ARBITRATION PROCEEDING WILL BE CONDUCTED ONLY ON AN INDIVIDUAL BASIS AND NOT IN A CLASS OR REPRESENTATIVE ACTION.
puzzles.title: Room for Only One
puzzles.question: On what basis, and not as a class or representative action, must any arbitration be conducted?
puzzles.riddle: My door opens only a crack, just wide enough for one. Crowds of the wronged may knock, but I let them in one at a time.
puzzles.plain_english: You cannot join other customers in a class action against Amazon; each person must bring their own claim in private arbitration. This makes it harder and less worthwhile to pursue small claims that affect many people.
hints: Look in the Disputes section, under the heading about class actions.
The capital-letter sentence says arbitration happens only on an '_____ BASIS'.

reasons.summary: Almost every dispute must go to binding arbitration instead of court, with a class-action waiver and a 60-day pre-arbitration negotiation requirement.
Anything you post gives Amazon a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free and fully sublicensable worldwide licence, and you must indemnify Amazon for claims over it.
Amazon can change these conditions at any time, and simply continuing to use the services counts as accepting the changes, with no notice period promised.
Amazon may refuse service, terminate accounts, remove content or cancel orders in its sole discretion.
Services are provided 'as is' and Amazon disclaims liability for damages of any kind to the extent the law permits.
If your chosen payment method fails, Amazon may charge any other valid payment method on your account.

twist.original:
We generally do not charge your credit card until after your order has entered the
shipping process or, for digital products, until we make the digital product available
to you.
twist.altered: We may charge your credit card at the time you place your order, before it has entered the shipping process or, for digital products, before we make the digital product available to you.
twist.question: Under the updated Pricing terms, when can Amazon now charge your card?
options: As soon as you place your order
Generally only once the order enters shipping
Only after the item is delivered
Only after the return window closes
twist.answer: As soon as you place your order
twist.plain_english: Charging at the moment of ordering instead of at shipping means your money can be tied up for items that are delayed, out of stock or later cancelled. Small timing changes like this are easy to miss but affect your cash flow and refunds.
